description: Everything that waits on a provider or on later work. A provider item is a working sandbox stand-in behind an interface; its service stays OFF for real users until the item is contract_signed (or live) for that country. `later` items are non-provider work that must happen before certain things go live. python3 providers/check.py keeps this honest: no stale entries, no unregistered placeholders, no service switched on without its provider.

later.name: Machine translation engine for every LynkOmni language (Google MADLAD-400-3B-MT, Apache 2.0)
later.why_not_now: Done 2026-11-07. The owner replaced Meta NLLB-200 (CC-BY-NC licence, no commercial use) with Google MADLAD-400-3B-MT (Apache 2.0). tools/translation/install_engine.py checks the licence, pins the model revision and converts it to CTranslate2 int8; the GitHub Actions workflow "translation" installs it (cached) and runs tools/translation/check_engine.py in every language. Because the 3B model was weak on short screen labels, screen text is translated by Claude (tools/translation/claude_packs.py, owner decision 2026-11-07); the engine is for text people type.
later.done_when: The engine is installed with a checked licence and pinned revision, knows every language in design/fonts/scripts.v1.json, every emulator has a current, fully translated pack for every language, and tests/test_layout_i18n.py passes in every language.

later.name: Translation engine running on LynkOmni's own server for text people type (chat messages, product names, notes)

Until the server exists, ContentTranslator has no engine, so typed text is shown in the original with the state "queued"; tests use SandboxTranslator.
later.done_when: The API server image installs ctranslate2 and sentencepiece and mounts the engine folder made by tools/translation/install_engine.py as LYNK_MT_DIR; ContentTranslator uses MadladTranslator there; typed text never leaves LynkOmni's servers.

later.why_not_now: Needs an address-format dataset vendored with a licence check; invoices and receipts print free-text address lines today.
later.done_when: Invoices, receipts and the shop page lay out addresses by the country's format.
later.blocks_note: polish of invoices and shop pages, not go-live

later.name: Calendar preferences per country (Hijri, Persian, Ethiopian, Buddhist beside Gregorian)
later.why_not_now: Needs the CLDR calendar-preference data wired through the locale layer; dates show Gregorian in every country today.
later.done_when: A country pack names its preferred calendars and screens show dates in the person's calendar, data unchanged.

later.name: Interface language waves (design/fonts/language_waves.v1.json)
later.why_not_now: 94 national official languages are not yet interface languages; one wave of ten is added per build section from section 3 on, with fonts, translations and the layout test.
later.done_when: Every national official language of every country is an interface language.
later.blocks_note: a country opens in its best supported language meanwhile

later.name: Country legal text, invoice numbering and holidays confirmed per country (rule 0.5 pack fields)
later.why_not_now: Each pack now carries holidays (from the holidays package, unconfirmed), the invoice numbering rules of services/invoicing.py (unconfirmed) and an empty legal_text. The legal wording on invoices and receipts must come from the country's lawyer, and holidays and numbering need a person in the country to confirm them.
later.done_when: For each country: its lawyer sets legal_text, a person confirms holidays and invoice numbering, and the three are marked confirmed; tools/country_holidays.py is re-run each January.
later.blocks_note: nothing legal is printed until set; holidays only inform schedules and reports

later.name: Lawyer review of the Storefront: marketplace terms, seller agreement, content policy, tax reporting, consumer law, copyright and data protection
later.why_not_now: Needs a lawyer in each launch country.
later.done_when: Written sign-off per country; paid Storefront selling switches on only after it.

later.name: LynkDriver signing key in secure hardware
later.why_not_now: Needs a hardware security module or a cloud key service under the company's account (section 14).
later.done_when: Every LynkDriver release is signed with the hardware-held key and devices refuse anything else.

later.name: Checks on physical devices (LynkDriver drivers and every interface version)
later.why_not_now: Needs sample devices; automatic checks already run on virtual devices and emulators.
later.done_when: Each device kind in the device register passed on a real unit.

later.name: Certified trackers, seals and safe-stop hardware
later.why_not_now: Needs a hardware supplier and certification per country; safe-stop works only through certified hardware.
later.done_when: Each tracker, seal and safe-stop unit is certified for its country and its LynkDriver driver is signed.

later.name: Police report pack format per country
later.why_not_now: Each country's police accept their own format; a person per country must confirm it.
later.done_when: Each country pack carries a confirmed report format.

later.name: Data-protection review of location data
later.why_not_now: A lawyer per region must confirm consent, retention and worker rules before positions are stored for owned assets and consenting workers.
later.done_when: Each region's retention and consent rules are confirmed and written into its country packs.

later.name: Trademark checks for LynkMotion, LynkGuard, LynkTrace, LynkGPS and LynkSentry
later.why_not_now: Needs the lawyer (owner action names-trademarks).
later.done_when: The five names are cleared or replaced.

later.name: LynkOmni's own map tiles, geocoding and offline region packs
later.why_not_now: Self-hosted open map data needs the cloud hosting of build section 14; emulators use labelled sample maps until then.
later.done_when: Map tiles, geocoding and offline packs are served from LynkOmni's own servers in every region cell.

later.name: The business successor rule, per country
later.why_not_now: Who may take over a business when its owner dies or is lost depends on each country's inheritance and company law; a lawyer must confirm the rule in each country first. Until then identity/protection.py shows the successor as coming soon.
later.done_when: A lawyer confirms the rule for a country and its country pack sets successor_confirmed true; identity/protection.py then offers it there.

user_actions.what: Approve workflow runs on pull requests opened by the brand-sync bot (button 'Approve workflows to run' on the pull request).
user_actions.why: GitHub does not run checks on bot pull requests until a person approves.

user_actions.what: Allow package installs in Claude's network settings, then start a new chat.
user_actions.why: Needed for font files and any library the interface emulators or tests may need later; until then everything is built without extra libraries. It also lets Claude install the NLLB-200 translation engine.
user_actions.done_note: Owner allowed package installs and Hugging Face for Claude Code cloud environments on 2026-11-06. The claude.ai chat workspace still blocks Hugging Face, so the translation engine is installed on GitHub Actions (workflow "translation") instead.

user_actions.what: Sign each provider in the ledger (card issuer, mobile money, banks, tax office, SMS, cloud) per country and send Claude the sandbox keys and documents.
user_actions.why: A service switches on for real users only when its provider is signed.

user_actions.what: Have a human designer review all visuals, icons and interface emulators.
user_actions.why: Everything is a draft until a designer signs off.

user_actions.what: Arrange a human security review of anything that moves money, sealing, card screens and agent services; later, an accredited auditor for SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001.
user_actions.why: Required before release by the LynkOmni rules.
user_actions.when: before any money feature goes live

user_actions.what: Arrange a human accessibility audit (WCAG 2.2 AA).
user_actions.why: Automatic checks are not a full audit.

user_actions.what: Have a lawyer check LynkOmni and product names, and register domains.
Create Apple Developer and Google Play developer accounts for the organisation.
user_actions.why: Needed to publish the real Android and iOS apps and capture store screenshots.

user_actions.what: Choose a supplier of Android handheld POS terminals with a built-in printer (and a counter tablet setup), and get two sample devices.
user_actions.why: The LynkPOS emulator shows an original LynkOmni design; the real app must be tested on the real terminals merchants will buy, and the supplier must allow our logo on the casing.
user_actions.when: On demand (BIZZ & DEVICE, 2026-11-09): only once people start ordering LynkOmni hardware. LynkOmni is digital first: every service runs on devices people already own, with compatible hardware from other makers through LynkDriver.

user_actions.what: Ask native speakers to check the words and screens in each language we launch with (Arabic, Persian, Urdu, Hebrew, Hindi, Swahili, Kinyarwanda, French, Spanish and others in design/fonts/scripts.v1.json).
user_actions.why: Fonts and right-to-left layout are in place, but translations written by Claude must be checked by people who speak the language before real users see them.
user_actions.when: before launching in a country that uses the language
user_actions.done_note: Owner decision 2026-11-06: no native-speaker review; machine translation (Google MADLAD-400; Meta NLLB-200 was replaced for licence reasons) with automatic protection and layout checks instead.

user_actions.what: Create the official LynkOmni accounts and claim the name on LinkedIn, X, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, WhatsApp Business, Snapchat, Pinterest and Threads; send Claude the links of the seven footer channels.
user_actions.why: Claiming the name everywhere stops others from impersonating LynkOmni; the footer links must lead to real, active accounts.
user_actions.done_note: Claimed as "LynkOmni" on all ten platforms on 2026-11-06; footer links connected (ts/src/footer.ts SOCIAL_LINKS); LinkedIn is a showcase page under the CruxOmni Group company page.

user_actions.what: Finish the company email: Google Workspace Business Starter (yearly, one paid user, billing country Cameroon) for cruxomni.com with the admin login marvin@cruxomni.com; then add lynkomni.com as a free second domain and the free addresses billing@, support@, hello@, security@lynkomni.com and legal@cruxomni.com. Then create the 28 Google Groups agreed on 2026-11-07 (master blueprint section 39), each with marvin@cruxomni.com as its member: on cruxomni.com accounts@, legal@, compliance@, finance@, investors@, press@, careers@, hello@; on lynkomni.com hello@, support@, billing@, security@, privacy@, safety@, accessibility@, partners@, agents@, accountants@, developers@, enterprise@, ads@, suppliers@; and postmaster@, abuse@ and dmarc-reports@ on each domain. Then add the SPF, DKIM and DMARC records Claude prepares, at Squarespace, for both domains.
user_actions.why: One Google platform for email and, later, hosting (owner decision 2026-11-06). The domains cruxomni.com and lynkomni.com were bought on Squarespace on 2026-11-07; Google refused the prepaid card, so payment needs a normal (not prepaid) Visa or Mastercard debit card with international online payments, or an official Google Workspace partner that accepts bank transfer or mobile money.
user_actions.result: Workspace paid; lynkomni.com verified as a secondary domain; all 28 addresses of catalog/contacts.v1.json exist as groups (postmaster@lynkomni.com reserved by Google); MX, SPF, DKIM (authenticating) and DMARC p=none live for both domains at Squarespace; DNSSEC on; delivery tested to hello@ and postmaster@lynkomni.com.

user_actions.what: Right after paying for Google Workspace (agreed 2026-11-07, email safeguards 1, 2, 5, 8 and 13): create a second super-admin account admin@cruxomni.com for emergencies only (one more paid user); turn on two-step verification with a passkey or physical security key, never SMS, on marvin@cruxomni.com and admin@cruxomni.com; switch on outside-sender warnings and the strongest phishing and malware protection; print the admin backup codes and keep them offline, with recovery email outside cruxomni.com (for example lynkomni@gmail.com) and your phone; turn on DNSSEC for both domains if Squarespace offers it. Claude writes the steps screen by screen.
user_actions.why: With one admin account, a hack or lock-out loses the company's email, Google Cloud and GitHub at once; Google recommends more than one super admin, and phishing-proof sign-in protects both.
user_actions.when: right after paying for Google Workspace
user_actions.result: admin@cruxomni.com is a second super admin; passkeys on both admins and two-step enforced; strong passwords 12+; third-party API access blocked; every alert rule active with email; Drive external sharing warned, access checker recipients only; Gmail safety at full with move-to-spam; backup codes offline and recovery contacts outside cruxomni.com for both admins.

user_actions.what: Optional, when you choose (email safeguard 6): buy a few look-alike domains (for example lynk-omni.com) and forward them to lynkomni.com so scammers cannot use them.
user_actions.why: Scammers register look-alike domains to trick merchants and customers.

user_actions.what: Register CruxOmni Group (with the lawyer), open a company bank account with a company card, get a free D-U-N-S number, then ask Google support to move the Workspace billing to the company and put the company as the owner of both domains.
user_actions.why: Needed for the Apple and Google developer accounts, startup cloud credits, payment providers and company invoices.
user_actions.when: with the lawyer, at the end of the owner's list

user_actions.what: Upgrade the LynkOmni GitHub organisation to the Team plan (billing email billing@lynkomni.com) and lock the main branch so changes can only enter through a pull request with green checks.
user_actions.why: Branch protection on private repositories needs a paid plan; until then the working standards are followed by hand.
user_actions.when: last item of the owner's list, after billing@lynkomni.com exists

user_actions.what: Open Google Cloud with the marvin@cruxomni.com login, add a payment method Google accepts and a budget alert; Claude then sets up hosting (Cloud Run, Cloud SQL, Cloud Storage through its S3-compatible connection) as code.
user_actions.why: LynkOmni's servers, language engine and offline sync need a home; one Google platform, pay as you go, no move needed as LynkOmni grows.
user_actions.when: when the merchant app is ready to go online

user_actions.what: Optional, 10 seconds per repository: GitHub -> lynkomni-platform and lynkomni-icons -> Settings -> Advanced Security -> Dependabot security updates -> Enable (the proxy cannot switch it on). Fix PRs for vulnerable dependencies then arrive as drafts and are merged under the dependency-updates rule.
user_actions.why: A free safety net on public repositories.
